Monolio Feature Tour

A sample document that shows Monolio's main features in one file. Tables, charts, math, diagrams (Mermaid), images, attachments, and multiple pages are all inside this single file.

Table of contents
1Text formatting1.1Five heading levels1.1.1Heading 3Heading 4Heading 52Lists and checks3Various blocks3.1Toggle heading (closed)A green heading (heading 4)4Tables that calculate5Charts6Math (TeX)7Diagrams (Mermaid)8Suggestions (proposed changes from people or AI)9Images and attachments10Multiple pages

1Text formatting

Plain text, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color, background color (highlighter), large text, a different typeface (Serif).

You can also write inline code such as npm run pwa:test and inline math such as E=mc2 or a2+b2.

Links: the Monolio repository. Pasting a URL turns it into a link: https://example.com/

Links to pages inside the text: type "@" and pick a page. For example, see Every kind of diagram (Mermaid) for the list of diagrams and Appendix for the appendix.

Links to blocks: take the link with "Copy link to block" (ブロックへのリンクをコピー) in the block handle menu and paste it into the text. Examples: Supply voltage: 24 V ± 10% , This table uses a header row,… . The page that is linked to (Specification details) shows the number of links pointing to it next to its title.

Dates in text: type "@today", "@tomorrow", "@2026-11-30", or "@11/30" (click a date to pick another one). Examples: the prototype is due on 2026年11月30日 , and the review meeting is on 2026年12月10日 .

Emoji: type ":" followed by an English name and suggestions appear (":smile" → 😄, ":warning" → ⚠️, ":white_check_mark" → ✅). Japanese names (":笑", ":注意") work too.

Zoom view: double-click an image, a Mermaid diagram, or a chart to show it full screen. Zoom with the wheel, move the view by dragging, and double-click to switch between "fit to screen" and 100% (the same in the saved HTML).

Pasting from other apps: copy blocks from Notion and paste them, and headings, bullets, to-dos, tables, toggles and so on arrive as blocks (the same for headings and lists from web pages and Google Docs).

Character count: Edit → 文字数… (Character count) shows the count for this page, the selected text, and the selected blocks (Japanese is counted one character at a time; line breaks are not counted, and the count without spaces is shown too). The block handle menu also shows the character count of that block at the bottom.

Markdown: File → Export as Markdown (Markdown に書き出す) writes all pages into one .md file (each page becomes "# Title", table formulas become their computed values, toggles become <details>, and images and attachments are written as names only). File → Import Markdown… (Markdown を読み込む…) brings a .md file in as new pages (a file that starts with "# " is split into pages at each "# ").

1.1Five heading levels

When View → Heading numbers (見出しに番号) is on, headings 1 to 3 get numbers such as 1 / 1.1 / 1.1.1 that run through the whole document, across pages (on in this sample). The numbers are not part of the heading text, so they are renumbered automatically when you reorder blocks or change heading levels. Headings 4 and 5 are not numbered.

// A code block (language: JavaScript)
function add(a, b) {

Code language and highlighting: click the language name at the top right of a code block to choose a language (JavaScript, Python, C/C++, Java, C#, Go, Rust, JSON, HTML, CSS, SQL, Bash, YAML, Markdown, and more). Typing "```python" also sets the language. The saved HTML uses the same colors.

# Python
@dataclass
class Part:
    name: str
    qty: int = 0

def total(parts):
    """Total stock"""
    return sum(p.qty for p in parts if p.qty > 0)
-- Total shipments
SELECT part_no, SUM(qty) AS total
FROM shipments
WHERE shipped_at >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY part_no
ORDER BY total DESC;

A table can also be a database (the "Database" button at the right end of the table toolbar). Give each column a type (text, number, date, select, check, link) and select values appear as colored tags, checks as boxes, and links as the title of another document. A link can also point to a page in the same document (enter the cell and choose "Choose a page…" (ページを選ぶ…); Ctrl+click jumps to that page). Links can be added to cells of an ordinary table too (enter the cell and use the link button above; see "Unit 2" in the table above).

Filters can use conditions too (enter a cell of the column, then "Filter" → "Condition" in the table toolbar). Number columns support = ≠ > ≥ < ≤ and ranges, text columns support "contains", "starts with" and so on, and date columns support "before", "after" and "on". Conditions set on several columns can be combined as "rows that match all columns (AND)" or "rows that match any column (OR)". 7Diagrams (Mermaid)

Diagrams are drawn from Mermaid code (insert with /mermaid or /図). The saved file contains the drawn diagram (SVG), so it can be viewed even without Mermaid.

コード
flowchart LR
  A[Start measurement] --> B{Temperature in range?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Record it]
  B -->|No| D[Raise a warning]
  C --> E[Next measurement]
  D --> E

図2: Processing flow (flowchart)

コード
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant P as Monolio
  participant F as Saved file
  U->>P: Write the diagram code
  P->>P: Draw the SVG with Mermaid
  U->>P: Save (Ctrl+S)
  P->>F: Write the SVG and the code
  Note over F: The diagram is visible without Mermaid

8Suggestions (proposed changes from people or AI)

This is a way to keep "what if we changed it like this" in the document without rewriting the text. In the panel on the right (the "Suggestions" (提案) button in the top bar), you can choose at any level (suggestion → table → column → single spot) and decide whether to accept or revert. You can also decide by hovering over a word or cell in the text. If the open file is rewritten from outside, for example by an AI, the difference also appears as a suggestion (rewrites you do not accept are reverted when you save). The paragraph and table below contain a suggestion from a pretend AI.

The test was run at a room temperature of 25℃, measuring 3 times under each condition.

📎Appendix

Before saving or sharing, "Check document…" (文書をチェック…) in the File menu (called "チェック" in the command palette) lists broken references, formula errors in tables, and mistakes in charts, diagrams, and math across all pages in the panel on the right. Click an item to jump to that place (even on another page or inside a closed toggle). After fixing, press "Re-check" (再チェック). The page below has problems put in on purpose.

🔍Document check practice

A page can have an icon (an emoji) above its title and a cover image. Use "Add icon" (アイコンを追加) and "Add cover" (カバーを追加), which appear when you hover over the title area. The icon also shows in the table of contents and in links to the page ("Appendix" has an example with a cover image).

The typeface of the whole document (standard, serif, monospace) and "Small text" are switched in the View menu (they are saved in the document, and the saved HTML and printing look the same).

A block can be moved to the end of another page with "Move to another page" (別のページへ移す) in the handle (⋮⋮) menu (child blocks go along; several selected blocks move together).

"Delete" for a page in the table of contents moves the page to the trash. From "Trash" at the bottom of the table of contents you can restore it or delete it permanently (this sample contains "Old memo". When you restore it, the link comes back right below this).

10.1Flowchart (flowchart)

Write steps and branches of a process. You can use box shapes (rectangle, diamond, cylinder, and so on) and groups (subgraph).

コード
flowchart TD
  subgraph Receiving inspection
    A[Receive the part] --> B{Dimensions within tolerance?}
  end
  B -->|Yes| C[To stock]
  B -->|No| D[(Defect record)]
  D --> E([Contact the supplier])

10.2Flowchart with ELK layout (flowchart-elk)

In Mermaid, this is a way to write a flowchart that is laid out with a method called ELK. The Mermaid bundled with Monolio does not include the ELK part (elkjs, whose license cannot be combined with the GPL), so it is drawn with the same layout as an ordinary flowchart. The way of writing is the same as a flowchart.

コード
flowchart-elk LR
  S1[Temperature sensor] --> C[Control board]
  S2[Emergency stop] --> C
  C --> M[Motor]
  C --> D[Display]
  C --> L[(Log)]
  D -.-> S2

10.3Sequence diagram (sequenceDiagram)

Write the exchanges between devices or programs in time order from top to bottom. Repeats (loop) and branches (alt) can be written too.

コード
sequenceDiagram
  participant PC as Control PC
  participant M as Instrument
  PC->>M: Start measurement (*TRG)
  activate M
  M-->>PC: Accepted
  loop 10 times
    M->>M: Sampling
  end
  M-->>PC: Measured value
  deactivate M
  alt Out of range
    PC->>PC: Record a warning
  else In range
    PC->>PC: Save the result
  end

10.4Class diagram (classDiagram)

Write the values and operations of software parts (classes) and the relations between them (inheritance, aggregation, and so on).

コード
classDiagram
  class Sensor["Sensor"] {
    +String model
    +read() float
  }
  class Thermocouple["Thermocouple"] {
    +String kind
  }
  class Logger["Logger"] {
    +save(value)
  }
  Sensor <|-- Thermocouple
  Logger "1" o-- "*" Sensor : connects

10.5State diagram (stateDiagram-v2)

Write the states of a device and what makes the state change.

コード
stateDiagram-v2
  state "Stopped" as Stop
  state "Standby" as Idle
  state "Running" as Run
  state "Fault" as Fault
  [*] --> Stop
  Stop --> Idle : Power on
  Idle --> Run : Start
  Run --> Idle : Stop
  Run --> Fault : Overcurrent
  Fault --> Stop : Reset

10.6ER diagram (erDiagram)

Write database tables (entities) and the relations between tables (one-to-many and so on).

コード
erDiagram
  DEVICE["Device"] {
    string id PK "Device number"
    string model "Model"
  }
  MEASUREMENT["Measurement"] {
    int id PK
    float value "Measured value"
    datetime at "Date and time"
  }
  OPERATOR["Operator"] {
    string name "Name"
  }
  DEVICE ||--o{ MEASUREMENT : "records"
  OPERATOR ||--o{ MEASUREMENT : "performs"

10.7User journey (journey)

Following the flow of work, write the satisfaction (1 to 5) at each stage and the people involved.

コード
journey
  title Experience of measurement work
  section Preparation
    Warm up the instrument: 3: Operator
    Calibration: 2: Operator, Quality staff
  section Measurement
    Measure: 5: Operator
    Copy the records: 1: Operator

10.8Gantt chart (gantt)

Write the schedule and the order of tasks (after means "after the previous task", crit marks an important task).

コード
gantt
  title Prototype schedule
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  axisFormat %m/%d
  todayMarker off
  section Design
    Circuit design :a1, 2026-10-01, 10d
    Board design :a2, after a1, 7d
  section Prototype
    Order parts :b1, 2026-10-08, 14d
    Assembly :b2, after a2, 5d
    Evaluation :crit, b3, after b2, 7d

Write the shares of a breakdown (showData also shows the values).

pie showData
  title Breakdown of defects
  "Solder defects" : 42
  "Wrong parts" : 18
  "Scratches" : 25
  "Other" : 15

10.10Quadrant chart (quadrantChart)

Place items into four areas using two axes (for example, ranking the priority of improvement ideas).

コード
quadrantChart
  title Priority of improvement ideas
  x-axis Low cost --> High cost
  y-axis Low effect --> High effect
  quadrant-1 Consider
  quadrant-2 Do now
  quadrant-3 Do later
  quadrant-4 Skip
  Add fixtures: [0.25, 0.8]
  Automatic inspection machine: [0.85, 0.75]
  Revise the work instructions: [0.15, 0.35]
  Replace the equipment: [0.9, 0.2]

10.11Requirement diagram (requirementDiagram)

Write requirements and the things that satisfy or verify them (SysML). Names must be alphanumeric; the descriptions (text and type) can be written in any language.

コード
requirementDiagram
  requirement temp_req {
    id: R1
    text: "Operating temperature is 0 to 40 °C"
    risk: medium
    verifymethod: test
  }
  functionalRequirement stop_req {
    id: R2
    text: "Stops within 1 second on a fault"
    risk: high
    verifymethod: test
  }
  element ctrl_board {
    type: "Control board"
  }
  element thermal_test {
    type: "Temperature test"
  }
  ctrl_board - satisfies -> temp_req
  ctrl_board - satisfies -> stop_req
  thermal_test - verifies -> temp_req

10.12Git graph (gitGraph)

Write the flow of branches, commits, and merges.

コード
gitGraph
  commit id: "First version"
  branch feature
  checkout feature
  commit id: "Measurement feature"
  commit id: "Add chart"
  checkout main
  commit id: "Fix typo"
  merge feature id: "v1.1" tag: "v1.1"

10.13C4 diagram (C4Context)

Write the relations between a system, its users, and external systems in the C4 model style (there are also levels such as C4Container).

コード
C4Context
  title Overview of the measurement system
  Person(op, "Operator", "Takes measurements")
  System(sys, "Measurement system", "Collects and records measured values")
  System_Ext(erp, "Production management system", "Receives the results")
  Rel(op, sys, "Operates")
  Rel(sys, erp, "Sends results", "HTTPS")

  2026 : Unit 2 released

10.16Sankey diagram (sankey-beta)

Show the flow of a quantity (power, cost, and so on) by the width of the bands. One line is "source,target,amount". Names must be alphanumeric only (this version of Mermaid cannot write Japanese here).

コード
sankey-beta
Power in,Controller,20
Power in,Motor,70
Power in,Loss,10
Motor,Mechanical out,60
Motor,Loss,10

10.17XY chart (xychart-beta)

Overlay bars and a line with axes. To draw from a table, the "Chart" block is a better fit.

コード
xychart-beta
  title "Monthly production"
  x-axis ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
  y-axis "Units" 0 --> 200
  bar [120, 150, 170, 160, 180, 190]
  line [110, 140, 165, 165, 175, 185]

10.18Block diagram (block-beta)

Decide the layout of the boxes yourself (number of columns, gaps) and write the structure.

コード
block-beta
  columns 3
  sensor["Sensor"] space ctrl["Control board"]
  space:3
  power["Power"] space motor["Motor"]
  sensor --> ctrl
  ctrl --> motor
  power --> ctrl

10.19Packet diagram (packet-beta)

Write how the bits of a communication frame or a register are assigned.

コード
packet-beta
  title Transmit frame
  0-7: "Start code"
  8-15: "Device number"
  16-31: "Measured value"
  32-39: "Status"
  40-47: "Checksum"

10.20Kanban (kanban)

Arrange tasks in columns such as "Not started, In progress, Done".

コード
kanban
  todo[Not started]
    t1[Design the fixture]
    t2[Revise the work instructions]
  doing[In progress]
    t3[Assemble prototype unit 2]
  done[Done]
    t4[Order the parts]

10.21Architecture diagram (architecture-beta)

Place servers, databases, and so on with icons (cloud, server, database, disk, internet) and write the connections.

architecture-beta
  group plant(cloud)[Factory]
  service pc(server)[Control PC] in plant
  service db(database)[Measurement data] in plant
  service disk1(disk)[Log] in plant
  service net(internet)[Company network]
  pc:R --> L:db
  db:B --> T:disk1
  pc:L -- R:net

10.22Radar chart (radar-beta)

Compare evaluations on several viewpoints with polygons.

radar-beta

10.25Fishbone diagram (ishikawa-beta)

Sort the causes of a problem into groups such as "People, Equipment, Materials, Methods" and draw them in a fishbone shape. The first line is the effect (the head).

  Dimensional defect

    Lot variation
  Materials
    Material variation
  Methods
    Processing conditions

Write a hierarchy of folders and files. Indentation shows the hierarchy, and a trailing / marks a folder (bold).

  measurements/
    2026-10/
      device1.csv
      device2.csv
    settings.json
  report.html

10.27Agent flow (agentflow-beta)

Write the flow of an AI agent's processing (input, task, tool, decision, output).

コード
agentflow-beta TB
  flow check["Inspection agent"]
    logs["Device logs"]@{ shape: input }
    analyse["Look for anomalies"]@{ shape: task }
    query["sql_query"]@{ shape: tool }
    ok["Anomaly found?"]@{ shape: decision }
    report["Send a report"]@{ shape: action }
    logs --> analyse --> query --> ok
    ok -- Yes --> report
  end

10.28Swimlane (swimlane-beta)

Write the flow of work divided into columns (lanes) for each department or owner.

コード
swimlane-beta LR
  subgraph design [Design]
    req[Decide the specification]
    draw[Draw the drawings]
  end
  subgraph make [Manufacturing]
    build[Assemble]
  end
  subgraph qa [Quality assurance]
    test{Pass the inspection?}
    ship([Ship])
  end
  req --> draw --> build --> test
  test -->|Yes| ship
  test -->|No| draw

10.29Railroad diagram (railroad-beta)

Show a grammar (syntax) in the shape of railway tracks. Combine parts such as terminal, nonterminal, choice, and optional.

コード
railroad-beta
title "Number"
number = sequence(optional(terminal("-")), oneOrMore(nonterminal("digit")), optional(sequence(terminal("."), oneOrMore(nonterminal("digit"))))) ;
digit = choice(terminal("0"), terminal("1"), terminal("9")) ;

10.30Railroad diagram from EBNF (railroad-ebnf-beta)

Turn a grammar written in EBNF into a railroad diagram (| is a choice, [ ] is optional).

コード
railroad-ebnf-beta
title "Command syntax"
command = "MEAS" , ":" , kind , [ "?" ] ;
kind = "VOLT" | "CURR" | "TEMP" ;

10.31Railroad diagram from ABNF (railroad-abnf-beta)

Turn a grammar written in ABNF (the notation used in RFCs) into a railroad diagram (1*4DIGIT means 1 to 4 digits).

コード
railroad-abnf-beta
title "Device number"
device-id = 2ALPHA "-" 1*4DIGIT ;

10.32Railroad diagram from PEG (railroad-peg-beta)

Turn a grammar written in PEG into a railroad diagram (/ is a choice tried in order, * and + are repeats).

コード
railroad-peg-beta
title "One line of settings"
Line <- Key "=" Value ;
Key <- Letter Letter* ;
Value <- Digit+ / "on" / "off" ;
Letter <- "a" / "b" / "z" ;
Digit <- "0" / "1" / "9" ;

10.33Wardley map (wardley-beta)

Place components on two axes, "visibility to the user (vertical)" and "maturity (horizontal)", and write dependencies and evolution (evolve). Wrap names in "".

コード
wardley-beta
title Structure of a measurement service
component "User" [0.95, 0.70]
component "Measurement app" [0.80, 0.45]
component "Analysis" [0.55, 0.30]
component "Cloud" [0.20, 0.85]
"User" -> "Measurement app"
"Measurement app" -> "Analysis"
"Analysis" -> "Cloud"
evolve "Analysis" 0.6

10.34Cynefin(cynefin-beta)

Place problems in five domains, "clear, complicated, complex, chaotic, confusion", and write the movement between domains with arrows.

コード
cynefin-beta
  title Classification of problem handling
  complex
    "Intermittent fault of unknown cause"
  complicated
    "Analyzing noise"
  clear
    "Replacing a fuse"
  chaotic
    "Smoke or fire"
  confusion
    "Waiting for a report of the symptoms"
  chaotic --> complex : "Secure safety"
  complex --> complicated : "Reproduced it"

10.35Use case diagram (usecase-beta)

Write the relations between users (actors) and what the system can do (use cases). Names (ids) must be alphanumeric; the displayed text can be written in any language.

コード
usecase-beta
direction LR
actor op("Operator")
actor admin("Administrator")
systemBoundary "Measurement system"
  measure("Measure")
  report("Create a report")
  calib("Calibrate")
end
op --> measure
op --> report
admin --> calib
measure ..> : include calib

10.36Kinds not included

Event modeling (eventmodeling) draws the text inside its boxes with HTML (foreignObject), so for safety Monolio removes the text and leaves empty boxes. For this reason it is not included in this sample.

ZenUML (zenuml) is not part of Mermaid itself (it is a separate add-on), so it cannot be drawn.
